Trench Excavation Checklist 8 checkpoints across 5 sections.Before drainage pipe laying Download ExcelDownload PDF **8** Checkpoints **5** Sections Per section QC Engineer, Drainage Supervisor [IS 1729:2017](https://infralens.in/code/IS-1729-1979) Related [📐IS 1729](https://infralens.in/code/IS-1729) [✏️Concrete cover](https://infralens.in/thumbrules/concrete-cover-by-exposure) [📘Excavation Rates & Quantiti…](https://infralens.in/handbook/excavation-rates) [📖Min cover for RCC](https://infralens.in/knowledge/minimum-cover-rcc-is-456) [🔧RCC design](https://infralens.in/tools/rcc-design) ### Checklist Preview Expand all ↓ | S.No. | Checkpoint | IS Requirement | Status | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A. TRENCH DIMENSION & DEPTH | | A1 | Trench width adequate for pipe OD + working space (min. 0.6 m each side of pipe)
Acceptance: Width ≥ Pipe OD + 1.2 m, measured at multiple points, documented | Cl. 5.1 — Width specification | | | A2 | Trench depth matches design (typically 0.5-2.0 m depending on street level and connections)
Acceptance: Depth measured at inlet/outlet/mid-span, matches design ±5cm, recorded on drawing | Cl. 5.2 — Depth verification | | | A3 | Invert level verified at design (elevation of pipe inside bottom); gradient slope per design
Acceptance: Invert level checked with theodolite, gradient 0.3-2.0% typical, documented | Cl. 5.3 — Invert level | | | B. TRENCH BOTTOM PREPARATION | | B1 | Trench bottom is firm and stable; no soft spots or mud; loose soil excavated and compacted
Acceptance: Bottom firm, no pooling water, no soft clay layers visible, CBR ≥5 preferred | Cl. 5.4 — Bottom condition | | | B2 | 100mm sand/gravel cushion layer placed on trench bottom for pipe support
Acceptance: Cushion layer 100mm, compacted, free from large stones, even distribution | Cl. 5.5 — Cushion layer | | | C. WATER MANAGEMENT | | C1 | Ground water level checked; if below invert, no additional dewatering needed; if above, sump/pumping arranged
Acceptance: GWT measured, if above invert: sump pump arranged, water controlled during laying | Cl. 5.6 — Groundwater control | | Showing 6 of 8 checkpoints ·View all → A. TRENCH DIMENSION & DEPTH A1Trench width adequate for pipe OD + working space (min. 0.6 m each side of pipe) Cl. 5.1 — Width specification (IS 1729) ✓ Width ≥ Pipe OD + 1.2 m, measured at multiple points, documented A2Trench depth matches design (typically 0.5-2.0 m depending on street level and connections) Cl. 5.2 — Depth verification (IS 1729) ✓ Depth measured at inlet/outlet/mid-span, matches design ±5cm, recorded on drawing A3Invert level verified at design (elevation of pipe inside bottom); gradient slope per design Cl. 5.3 — Invert level (IS 1729) ✓ Invert level checked with theodolite, gradient 0.3-2.0% typical, documented B. TRENCH BOTTOM PREPARATION B1Trench bottom is firm and stable; no soft spots or mud; loose soil excavated and compacted Cl. 5.4 — Bottom condition (IS 1729) ✓ Bottom firm, no pooling water, no soft clay layers visible, CBR ≥5 preferred B2100mm sand/gravel cushion layer placed on trench bottom for pipe support Cl. 5.5 — Cushion layer (IS 1729) ✓ Cushion layer 100mm, compacted, free from large stones, even distribution C.
